name: Routing correctness over the classification cases
purpose: The router's whole job over the classification cases, a share held out: route (answer, tool, deep, confirm, clarify), the tool, the arguments it fills in, every tool of a multi-step request, no confirming argument on a first destructive ask, no tool call where no change was asked Read in this direction: maximise correct route, tool and argument choice over labelled cases; minimise deep runs launched for plain questions, destructive requests sent without confirmation, and tool calls made where no change was asked; minimise model spend per routed message. Measured planner failures: a paraphrased current-state update sent to deep or answered, and a mass destructive request sent to deep without a confirm. The pre-route is not decided here (pre_route_then_planner is the operate-a-quest stack measured on routing only and ties the planner at no lower cost).
record: The pass rate, passed cases out of cases run, of each implementation on the same cases, with the recorded cost as the tie-break; each run is one row of the results file pinned to the commit and the cases hash, and the leaderboard compares rows only when the hash matches.

name: Update-offering correctness over synthetic quest channels
purpose: synthetic quests across the quest channels (notes, goal updates, decisions): the exact set of items offered and of open asks (own words offered, assistant echoes and unattributed notes left out, answered and already-seen items not repeated, age and count bounds) Read in this direction: raise the share of new human-authored items offered exactly once; lower the count of repeated, already-answered, self-echoed or unattributed items offered. Covers the quest channels only; Drive, inbound mail, Notion and chat sources need real accounts. The cases state rules the code already follows, so passing is a regression pin, not evidence a rule is right.

name: Exactly-once mid-run delivery per run, and how fast it is seen
purpose: synthetic cases: a message pushed before or during a run reaches the next planner decision once, only for its own conversation, and is never silently lost (through a real Orchestrator), plus the inbox port contract. For a deep worker with a live session, offline against a scripted stand-in for Claude Code: each message is written once and only to its own run (two concurrent runs never cross), a message landing as the run finishes is delivered once or left unclaimed, a message written but not confirmed seen is handed back as unseen, an ignored interrupt ends in terminate then kill, and work finished before a stop or pause is present when the session resumes. Measured on top, with real runs: send-to-seen latency, acted-on share, stop-to-quiet time and cost per run Read in this direction: cut the time from send to seen. A distributed inbox (for example Redis) is a consumer's and is not compared, and the loop cases cover the planner's drain points only. The live deep-worker session is pinned offline against a scripted stand-in, which cannot show latency, acted-on share, stop-to-quiet time or cost; the task and chat surfaces still claim through a 15 s throttle outside a live session.
record: The pass rate, passed cases out of cases run, of the live implementation on the rule's cases, recorded as a row of the results file pinned to the commit and the cases hash; a rule holds or does not, so the implementations are never ranked and a deliberately broken baseline must fail the same cases. The measured part is recorded per arm (the one-shot subprocess runner and the stream_json runner on the same cases) as one row each: pass rate on the floor cases, send-to-seen latency p50 and p90 in seconds (from the push to the model receiving the message: the planner prompt, or the worker's replay of it), acted-on share (steer cases whose required change happened, checked by a deterministic file or command check, no judge), stop-to-quiet time p90 (stop request to the last tool event), lost-work incidents (must be zero) and cost per run in dollars. The one-shot arm scores its latency as the end of the run by construction.
cascading_conditionals: offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=the in_memory offline arm of receive_input_mid_run runs the whole case set with no model call]

purpose: offline cases of image-bearing requests answered with and without the description: maximise the pass-rate gain the description gives on those cases (value), at a cost per image below the cost of the answer it informs and a description time that does not hold the turn longer than the person would wait; an image whose description changes no verdict is cost without value and counts against it.
